newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chirac, Kohl meet again on European reform.
newsitem.headline: Chirac, Kohl meet again on European reform.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac and German Chancellor Helmut Kohl met for the second time in four days on Tuesday to hammer out joint positions on the road to a single European currency and reform of the European Union.
But the two leaders cancelled plans for a joint statement after the talks, which were interrupted by news of a bomb attack in a Paris underground station which killed two people.
Chirac instead made a brief televised statement condemning the attack and expressing sympathy for the victims and their families.

An official in Chirac's office told reporters that both leaders used the talks to prepare for a Franco-German summit in Nuremberg, Germany, on Monday and a European Union summit in Dublin later this month.
"The President and the Chancellor are determined to do everything they can together to ensure the success of the Nuremberg and Dublin meeetings," the official said.

He declined specific comment on whether Chirac and Kohl had hammered out common ground on an EU budget discipline pact meant to prevent members of European monetary union running up big deficits after the launch of the euro in 1999.

On Monday, EU finance ministers' talks on the pact foundered on German insistence that there be strict numerical definitions laying out the exceptional circumstances -- such as severe recession -- which would exempt countries paying fines if they ran up excessively large deficitis.
Officials said on Monday however that the finance ministers made progress on the pact and said they were optimistic an agreement could be reached at the Dublin summit on December 13 and 14.
Finance ministers will meet again on the eve of the summit.
One diplomat said however that Paris and Bonn were essentially in agreement on the issue.
Germany, which has been isolated in its insistence on numerically definitions for exemptions from fines, would eventually settle for a less precise formula, the diplomat said.

The two leaders met in the French town of Perigueux on Saturday for an informal meeting after which Chirac reaffirmed France's commitment to a stable parity between the franc and the mark in the run up to economic and monetary union in 1999.
